description: We are engineering beginner students passionate about human spaceflight, telemetry software, and building practical digital tools for deep-space health monitoring. Join Team OrbitOS if you are interested in frontend development, space physiology research, UI/UX design, or video editing and storytelling to help bring our space-health software concept to life!
summary: ASTRA-MED is an offline-capable space-health monitoring and longitudinal trend analysis application built for astronauts on long-duration deep-space missions where communication delays prevent real-time Earth medical consultation. By combining an interactive 4-system anatomical bio-telemetry map, guided microgravity self-measurement checklists, day-over-day delta detection, and sourced NASA Human Research Program (HRP) educational references, ASTRA-MED enables non-physician crew members to recognize physiological and behavioral shifts early and export structured Flight Surgeon telemetry packets. Prominent simulation indicators, data provenance tags, and threshold citations ensure scientific transparency while clarifying that educational guidance supports—rather than replaces—qualified flight surgeons.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS:

ASTRA-MED is an autonomous astronaut health telemetry and longitudinal trend analysis web application designed for long-duration deep-space missions. It tracks seven physiological and behavioral indicators—Resting Heart Rate, complete Blood Pressure (Systolic/Diastolic), Respiratory Rate, Blood Glucose, Body Temperature, Sleep Duration, and Mood/Focus Index—alongside an interactive 4-system anatomical bio-telemetry map (Neurological/Circadian, Cardiovascular, Respiratory/Cabin Atmosphere, and Metabolic/Immune).

Rather than relying on isolated single-day snapshots, the Mission Health Intelligence engine compares current readings against both the previous mission day and a rolling 7-day baseline. When significant shifts occur, it highlights previous vs. current values, explains the longitudinal trend, and suggests structured next steps for qualified medical review. Crew members can compare any two mission days side-by-side via the Health History Timeline, inspect the spaceflight and clinical origin of every advisory threshold, and export a structured JSON Flight Surgeon Report containing timestamps, deltas, rolling averages, and data provenance tags.

BENEFITS, CREATIVITY & DESIGN FACTORS:

On lunar or Mars transits, 14–22 minute communication delays prevent real-time Earth medical consultation. ASTRA-MED empowers non-physician crew members with zero-G self-measurement checklists and visual body-system mapping while maintaining strict scientific transparency: a prominent simulation banner and provenance tags distinguish synthetic NASA HRP-modeled baselines from manual entries and simulated stress scenarios, framing all guidance as sourced educational references rather than clinical diagnoses.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & IMPACT:

Built with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and Lucide React, and deployed on Netlify (https://astra-med-2026.netlify.app). It runs 100% client-side with local persistence for offline spacecraft reliability, with future applications in polar research stations, submarines, and rural telemedicine.
